records.issue_text: [BUG] runShardSplitQuery calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables with a third argument (request.filters) that the method's signature does not accept. LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables is declared as (query: LokiQuery, scopedVars: ScopedVars) => LokiQuery; passing request.filters is a TS2554 too-many-arguments compile error, breaking the Loki datasource build and every CI type-check job on this branch. The diff provides no change to the datasource signature accepting filters, so the call site is invalid as written.

records.issue_text: [BUG] runSplitQuery applies template variables to queries without clearing/normalizing downstream fields, unlike the prior shard path which used interpolateVariablesInQueries which also sets intervalMs and maxDataPoints via template interop. Metric queries routed through runSplitQuery previously reached execution with variables already replaced upstream by the datasource's query() path; the new in-place applyTemplateVariables here mutates the shared request.targets objects (applyTemplateVariables returns the same query object it mutates in Loki's implementation), so subsequent consumers of the original request (partial-update bookkeeping, non-splitting query list) observe interpolated state — behavior change with no upstream test asserting idempotency when both the datasource and runSplitQuery interpolate the same target.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] runShardSplitQuery now interpolates each target via applyTemplateVariables at entry, while the updated test 'Interpolates queries before running' still expects 5 applyTemplateVariables calls for a single-query request, proving the shard-splitting internals also interpolate the already-interpolated queries. Template interpolation runs twice on the same expr; any non-idempotent substitution (a variable whose value contains '$', chained/nested variables, or format modifiers) produces a corrupted selector sent to Loki. Whoever uses shard splitting with such variables gets wrong or empty results.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] runSplitQuery adds interpolation with no counterpart change to the non-splitting execution path shown in the diff, so the change is only traceable to the new tests, not to any stated requirement about where interpolation belongs. If the surrounding query pipeline already interpolates before invoking runSplitQuery (as the Loki datasource does for direct queries), queries taking the split path are interpolated twice; maintainers bitten by a variable rendering bug will find two interpolation sites to reconcile.

This is a substantive pipeline/architecture change (where interpolation happens) that could create duplication if callers already interpolate, but the existence of an upstream interpolation step is not verifiable from this diff. records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] runSplitQuery now unconditionally interpolates targets, but the Loki datasource's main `query()` entry point also interpolates targets before dispatch, so queries reaching the split path from the normal pipeline get interpolated twice. If `LokiDatasource.query()` (the production caller of runSplitQuery/runShardSplitQuery) already calls `interpolateVariablesInQueries`/`applyTemplateVariables` on `request.targets` before delegating, this map is a second pass over already-interpolated strings. The tests only exercise runSplitQuery called directly with raw targets, so the double-interpolation behavior in the real entry path is untested and any variable value containing `$`-patterns from user data gets silently mangled. Needs verification that the split entry point is only ever reached with un-interpolated targets (e.g. called before the query()-level interpolation), which this diff does not establish.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] runSplitQuery now interpolates queries before splitting, but the same queries are still handed to datasource.runQuery, which interpolates again on its normal path — introducing double template-variable application that never existed for this code path. Previously runSplitQuery deliberately passed raw exprs through and let the execution layer interpolate exactly once; after this change any query where interpolation is not idempotent (escaped variables like $${var}, nested ${a${b}} forms, or $step formats like $__rate_interval whose second pass re-expands against the already-substituted range) is interpolated twice, yielding corrupted exprs for users of split queries. The test added in this diff only asserts the happy-path single-pass idempotent case ('$step' -> '5m' -> '5m'), so the drift is unverified.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The updated 'Interpolates queries before running' test asserts only the mock's invocation count (toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)) for applyTemplateVariables, not that the interpolated results propagate to the actual runQuery payloads. The count assertion verifies the mock was invoked, not the behavior — if the pipeline dropped the returned query objects and executed the raw request.targets instead, the count check still passes while users see un-interpolated expressions; the toHaveBeenCalledWith runQuery assertion that follows partially mitigates this only for one call shape.
